block.heading: Booking.com listings rebuilt to rank higher and convert more
paragraphs: We work to bring your Booking.com content score to 100%, keeping your existing reviews intact. As part of our OTA optimization, we update your title, description, photos, policies and amenity tags, refine your room content, choose your main photo and set your gallery order. We also set up your rate plans, Genius and promotions, with policies built around conversion.

We make every change live in your extranet with you on Zoom. Listings we optimize usually rise in Booking.com search rankings within 2 to 4 weeks: 7 of the 10 we optimized in 2025 did, by weekly position on fixed searches.

block.heading: Distribution Strategy Built Around Your Hotel
paragraphs: We build your hotel distribution strategy around your property. We place your inventory across online travel agencies and your own direct booking channels to grow your online presence.

items.heading: One live inventory pool
paragraphs: Your OTAs and your direct booking engine all draw from one shared room count through your channel manager. There are no separate OTA blocks or manual extranet updates, which in our experience keeps overbooking risk low.

items.heading: Near sell-out controls
paragraphs: When a date gets close to selling out, we close your highest-commission channels first with stop-sells and closed-to-arrival restrictions. Your direct channel stays open until the last room.

items.heading: Pricing integration safeguards
paragraphs: When you also use our [Dynamic Pricing Strategy](/dynamic-pricing-strategy/), we pause automation as soon as there's a sync fault. We fix a fault in our own RateHarbor setup within 4 hours and tell you about it the same day. If it sits in your PMS, channel manager or an OTA, we find it, report it and coordinate with that provider; how long the repair takes depends on them. If more than 12 hours pass without fresh data, we hold your verified rates. After syncing is restored, we reconcile any bookings made during the outage within 24 hours.

items.heading: Approved spending limits
paragraphs: We propose a monthly budget and how to split it across channels. We keep spending within the limit you approve and never raise it without your written approval.

items.heading: Campaigns and measurement
paragraphs: [Hotel Digital Marketing](/hotel-digital-marketing/) covers campaign structure, weekly bid adjustments, monthly reviews and conversion tracking. If vendor-installed tags are required, we make a test booking within 5 business days. You also get a 30-day report.

block.heading: Revenue Management Services, from Daily Pricing to Owner Reports
paragraphs: We take responsibility for your revenue work from strategy through implementation and ongoing optimisation, so you don't have to build an in-house revenue team.

items.heading: Strategy agreed with you
paragraphs: We build your revenue strategy around your hotel or resort and the occupancy, ADR and RevPAR goals you set. Then we turn our findings into improvement plans you can act on.

items.heading: Clear decision boundaries
paragraphs: On the monthly retainer, we decide daily rates, restrictions and inventory within guardrails we agree with you. You keep full control of pricing, see every rate and channel and make major decisions together with us, and we never overwrite a manual rate override you set.

items.heading: Competitive market monitoring
paragraphs: We track your competitive set alongside market trends. That way your pricing and rate strategy is based on competitor benchmarks and demand signals instead of your property's performance in isolation.

items.heading: Your pricing control
paragraphs: You keep full control of pricing and can see every rate and channel. We make major decisions together with you and keep disruption to your team to a minimum.

items.heading: Check before signing
paragraphs: Before you sign, we send you an anonymised sample monthly report. Look at how it explains rate changes, results and forecasts against actuals, not just the KPIs. That shows you how you'll hold us accountable.

items.heading: Sample daily snapshot
paragraphs: You also get a sample daily snapshot. It shows changes from the last 24 hours, a day-by-day view of the next 12 months and competitors' rates for context.

items.heading: Scope changes
items.text: We price any work outside your agreed scope separately, and we only start it once you've agreed to it in writing.

items.heading: Separate provider costs
items.text: Budget separately for OTA commissions, software subscriptions and any advertising or metasearch spend. These aren't part of our fee. You pay them directly to the providers.

items.heading: Optional ongoing advice
items.text: Once your starter or core engagement ends, you can choose to take a monthly advisory retainer. It includes a monthly strategy check-in, quarterly planning and asynchronous advice by message or email.

items.heading: Retainer decision support
items.text: You get insights from comparable hotel clients. When a major decision comes up, you also get priority access to our team.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: What will my team need to give you, such as account access and brand assets? And which ads and content do I have to approve, and how often?
items.answer: You'll give us your property details, logo, brand guidelines and photo library. You'll also give us user access to your website, booking engine, email platform and the ad accounts your property owns, and join us for a 60-minute kickoff call. No ad, listing text or other content goes live until you've approved it in writing. We send you one batch to approve each week and ask you to reply within 2 business days.

items.question: Which choices change your marketing service fee: managed channels, media spend, content volume, website scope, integrations or language versions?
items.answer: Your fixed monthly retainer depends on how many channels we manage and how much content we produce each month. Website projects, system integrations and extra language versions are one-time fees, set out in your written proposal. Media spend doesn't change our fee. You pay ad and metasearch platforms directly with your own payment method, separately from our fee, and we take no percentage.

items.question: Can we commission selected marketing channels without buying the full marketing service or your revenue management service?
items.answer: Yes. You can commission paid search, SEO, email or any other single channel without taking full marketing or revenue management. Revenue management, OTA management and our related online services are available separately or together. If you choose several, we bundle them and give you priority turnaround.

items.question: If you build me a new direct-booking website, how long until it is live, and how soon do campaigns start?
items.answer: We launch a new direct-booking website, or updates to your existing site, in 4 to 6 weeks. Nothing is published until you've signed it off in writing. Ad campaigns start within 10 business days of us getting account access and your approval. Until launch they run against your current site. Bookings traced to paid search and SEO showed within 60 to 90 days for 5 of the 7 hotels we ran both for in 2025; SEO rankings, tracked weekly on fixed searches, usually keep building for 6 to 12 months. We don't guarantee results.

items.question: What minimum media budget is needed for you to manage paid search or metasearch meaningfully, and which would you recommend if we cannot fund both?
items.answer: For paid search, your budget needs to cover about 30 clicks a day on your key search terms. For metasearch, it needs to keep bids live every day across at least 90 days of stay dates. We launch either channel only when the funding keeps it running without gaps. If you fund one channel, metasearch comes first and paid search second. Metasearch reaches travellers who are already comparing rates, and your spend follows actual clicks or bookings. You pay media spend directly to each platform, outside our fee.

items.question: Can you take over our existing advertising accounts and campaigns while preserving their history and working around channels still managed by our current agency?
items.answer: Yes. You add a named login for us to your existing ad and metasearch accounts, which preserves your campaign history, conversion data and bidding history. We review the accounts for 1 to 2 weeks before we change anything. Where your agency keeps some channels, we agree in writing at the start who owns each channel and task, and we work alongside them to minimise disruption.

items.question: Which languages can you support for campaigns, website content and guest emails, including localisation rather than translation alone?
items.answer: We create campaigns, website content and guest emails in both English and French. We write and adapt each one for its market instead of translating word for word. For other languages, you supply the translations, and we adapt the layouts, currencies, date formats and offers to the market.

items.question: After launch or optimisation, do you maintain website content, software and booking links, or must our team or web developer handle those tasks?
items.answer: While your monthly programme runs, we maintain your website through the user access you give us. That covers up to 4 content updates a month, software and plugin updates within 5 business days of their release, and a check of your booking-engine links once a week. If you keep a developer or agency, we agree in writing at the start who owns each task.

block.heading: Tracking Results Against Your Competitive Set
paragraphs: If your hotel subscribes to paid market-share data, we track three indexes from it against your competitive set: occupancy (MPI), ADR (ARI) and RevPAR (RGI). Without that data, we compare competitor rates, booking pace and pickup instead, and label those comparisons as estimates, never as MPI, ARI or RGI. Managed levels show them in weekly and monthly reports and an in-depth quarterly review. An index at your competitive set's level means you're matching it, and a higher index means you're gaining share.

We judge pricing mainly by how those measures move, not by occupancy or ADR alone. We compare your results with the same period last year and with your budget, which separates pricing performance from seasonality and wider market movement. That's why managed levels review and update your competitive set with you every quarter, and a self-run setup at each paid revisit.

block.heading: Who RateHarbor Is and How We Forecast Demand
paragraphs: We build your demand calendar 12 months ahead from at least 12 months of your booking history, or 24 months if you have it. We combine your booking patterns with market evidence to classify demand, and we revise the calendar as new signals appear.

Some events are announced late and others never appear on public calendars, so the calendar is a working document rather than a fixed forecast. If your booking history is short or patchy, your initial calendar is less reliable and leans more heavily on market data.

As your [outsourced hotel revenue and OTA management company](/about-us/), RateHarbor assigns you one dedicated specialist from our 12-person team. Your specialist has at least 5 years of experience with independent and boutique hotels. Each specialist handles no more than 10 properties, and the team covers you all 365 days of the year.

block.heading: Weeks 1 to 4: Diagnosing What Makes You Distinctive
paragraphs: In weeks 1 to 4, we base your positioning on booking evidence, not instinct.

steps.heading: Collect booking history
steps.text: You send us at least 12 months of booking history, or 24 months if you have it. Export it from your PMS by date, room type, channel and rate code.

steps.heading: Gather guest evidence
steps.text: We use whatever data you have on guest origins, lengths of stay, lead times and review scores, alongside competitive analysis and guest research.

steps.heading: Label missing evidence
steps.text: We fill any gaps with comp-set rates, market demand data and your budget. We mark these figures as estimates and revisit the diagnostic as your own data replaces them.

steps.heading: Identify distinctive strengths
steps.text: We compare your design, location, views and signature room types against your reviews and bookings to establish what guests value.

steps.heading: Define guest segments
steps.text: From the evidence we've collected, we identify 3 to 4 target segments, such as weekend couples or design-minded travellers.

steps.heading: Translate positioning into pricing
steps.text: We set base rates, rate floors and room-type differentials and price your distinctive rooms at a premium. We also match rate plans, minimum stays and packages to how each segment books.

block.heading: Client results

items.text: For a 34-room independent motel in Ontario, we rebuilt its OTA listings, fixed rate parity and launched direct-booking search campaigns. From March 2024 to February 2025 against the previous 12 months, its share of room nights booked direct rose from 9% to 21%, and its Booking.com content score (the extranet's own listing score) went from 62% to 100%.

For a 42-room independent boutique hotel in Cornwall, we realigned pricing, OTA presence and direct booking with the owner's new upscale positioning. In April–September 2025 against the same months of 2024, its RevPAR index (its RevPAR ÷ its competitive set's) rose from 0.93 to 1.07, and its share of room nights booked direct went from 14% to 26%.

For a three-hotel independent city-centre group in Queensland, we combined forecasting, pricing and channel strategy across the portfolio and sent the owners monthly reports. In 2025 against 2024, the three hotels' combined RevPAR index (their RevPAR ÷ their competitive sets') rose from 0.97 to 1.09, and their share of room nights booked through OTAs fell from 68% to 55%.

rows: Channel mix and differentials
We decide which OTAs get more weight and when. We manage rate differentials so that no channel suppresses your rank or undercuts your direct rate.
Undercutting alert

Leaking rates

OTA-funded discounts

Verification after changes

Direct-booking incentives

paragraphs: If you tie each resource to its decision deadline, you'll have time to act before demand, OTA rankings or budgets are locked in.

items.heading: Free resource access
items.text: Every guide, template and checklist is free, and each card above shows a sample of it. Request the ones you want on the form, and we'll email the full files.

items.heading: Peak season pricing
items.text: Use the rate strategy guide 8 to 12 weeks before your peak season, because that's when it's most useful.

items.heading: Year-round demand
items.text: If your demand is fairly even with no clear peak, seasonal timing gives you less value. In that case, review your rates on a steady rolling schedule.

items.heading: Listing refresh preparation
items.text: Go through the OTA listing checklist before any listing refresh and use it to guide your changes.

items.heading: Financial year preparation
items.text: Use the budget template about 3 months before your financial year starts.

items.heading: Month-end reporting
items.text: Use the performance report template at each month-end close to review your results.

block.heading: How Our Remote Team Works
paragraphs: The team has three groups: revenue management, OTA management and owner reporting. Each account has one dedicated specialist, so owners always deal with someone they know. When you're on vacation or in training, colleagues who know the account cover your properties. Pricing and listings need attention every day, so part of your week goes on handover notes and shared updates. Some people find this coordination work less rewarding than direct client work.

Your core hours are 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday to Friday. You get 20 paid vacation days a year and weekly internal training and knowledge-sharing sessions. We also give you paid time to take revenue management certification courses.

visuals.caption: Sharing account updates so colleagues can cover confidently.

block.heading: How to Apply: From Application to Offer
paragraphs: Job titles vary, so we judge your practical work, not just your CV, across three video-call steps over about 3 weeks.

steps.heading: Send Your Application
steps.text: Email your CV and a short note saying which role you want to the address on our [contact page](/contact-us/).

steps.heading: Introductory Video Call
steps.text: The video-call process starts with a 30-minute introductory call, which comes before the practical exercise.

steps.heading: Practical Property Exercise
steps.text: You spend 2 hours on pricing or listings for a sample property. These 2 hours show us how you work more clearly than an interview answer does.

steps.heading: Final Team Interview
steps.text: After you finish the practical exercise, you meet two team members for the final interview.

steps.heading: Decision Or Offer
steps.text: Within 5 business days of the final interview, we send you a decision or a written offer.

block.heading: Choose Your Service Level and Room-Count Tier
paragraphs: Your service level depends on how much time your team has for daily pricing and channel work. We start with onboarding to set up the groundwork, then agree on a monthly programme.
rows: Managed pricing
We manage your pricing as a standalone service or as part of fully outsourced revenue management. If you choose pricing alone, your team keeps OTA and channel decisions.
Pricing and optimisation
We combine managed pricing with channel and segment optimisation.
Full revenue management
We handle daily pricing, OTAs and reporting. This broader service needs deeper system access and closer coordination with your team.
Setup and onboarding
We set up your competitor set, rate structure and baseline for the ongoing work. Your written proposal states the setup fee, which is a one-time, non-recurring charge.
Room-count tiers
Monthly hotel revenue management plans are priced in three tiers: 40 rooms or fewer, 41 to 120 rooms, and more than 120 rooms.

block.heading: Bundle Several Services With Priority Turnaround
paragraphs: If you need several one-time services now, request them together. We'll bundle them, put them in the right order and give them priority turnaround. Coordinating work that depends on other work, such as pricing-tool setup and OTA listing optimisation, avoids rework and conflicting settings. Bundling only pays off when you need those services now. If you need a single urgent fix, order it on its own.
